title: Ferry routes
scenario: Ferry stops are joined by one-way routes. Starting at the depot, can you reach the lighthouse?

intro.job: Ferry stops are joined by one-way routes. Starting at the depot, can you reach the lighthouse?

idea.rule: The seen set is the memory — without it, the walk goes in circles forever.
idea.detail: The adjacency dict IS the map: each stop lists the stops its routes lead to. To ask 'can I get there?', walk from the start: if you're at the target, yes; otherwise try each route out, and ask the same question from there. But routes can loop back — harbor leads back to depot — and a walk with no memory follows the loop forever. Keep a set of the stops you've already been to, and never walk into one again.

model_restatement: Say whether some chain of one-way routes leads from the start stop to the target stop.

clarify.question: Can the routes loop back on themselves?
clarify.answer: Yes — harbor leads back to depot. Your walk has to survive that.

clarify.question: What if there's no way to reach the target?
What about a stop with no routes out?
clarify.answer: It's a dead end — like the cliff. Just try the next route.

clarify.question: Do I need the shortest path or the actual route?
clarify.answer: No — just whether you can get there: True or False.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: To reach the target from a stop: if this stop is the target, yes. Otherwise try each route out of it, and ask the same question from where it leads. If none works, no.

checkpoints.prompt: The first call reaches line 2. Which stop is node?
The walk takes its first route. On the next call, which stop is node?
With the fix — after the second stop is remembered, what is seen?

why_line: The draft has no memory: depot → market → harbor → back to depot, and round again, forever. Python would stop it with a RecursionError; here the tracer stops it after 2000 steps — the lighthouse is never reached.

explain.rule: A walk with no memory is a tourist with no map marks — at the harbor, the road back to the depot looks as good as any, so it goes round and round.
explain.bridge: The walk goes depot → market → harbor → depot. What would it need to know at the harbor to take the cove road instead?

fix.rule: Carry a seen set: add each stop as you leave it, and never walk into a stop that's already in it.

walk.gloss: The first call starts an empty memory...
Remember this stop before walking on.
Only walk to stops not already seen.

contrast.wrong: for nxt in graph[node]: if can_reach(...)
contrast.right: if nxt not in seen and can_reach(..., seen)

alternatives.note: The same walk with an explicit to-do list instead of recursion — the seen set does the same job.

hints: Follow the draft from depot. Where does the harbor's first route lead?

Pass a seen set along: seen.add(node), and only walk to nxt if nxt not in seen.

follow_up.fix_hint: The seen set lets it walk past the loop — cove → light → harbor → depot → market → cliff.
